reason: The cited evidence only generally notes the room-temperature brittleness of RHEAs (E3) and mentions irradiation resistance in other W-based RHEAs (E1), but provides no specific support for the claimed HCP phase formation, toughening mechanisms, or irradiation benefits in NbMoTaW with Ti/Zr additions. E2 and E4 are irrelevant to the proposed intervention.
premises: Ti or Zr additions (~5–10 at.%) will form a dual-phase BCC+HCP microstructure in NbMoTaW
The HCP phase activates extra slip systems and enables transformation-induced toughening, improving room-temperature ductility
The HCP phase enhances defect recombination under irradiation, improving irradiation tolerance
The dominant BCC phase preserves the high-temperature strength of NbMoTaW up to 1600 °C
The dual-phase microstructure reduces helium blistering compared to single-phase BCC NbMoTaW
